title: Training Notes: Background Check Recency and Temporary For-Hire Permits
content:
These notes cover a rule of the **Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing** product: how recent a Wayfare driver's latest clear background check is bears on the temporary permit acceptance days, the calendar days from the upload day for which a temporary for-hire permit is accepted as the for-hire permit on file.

**Rule.** When the latest clear background check on the agreement is dated fewer than 180 calendar days before the upload day, the temporary permit acceptance days gain 6 days; when it is dated at least 180 but fewer than 365 days before, they gain 3 days; when it is dated 365 days or more before, they gain none.

| Background check date, counted back from the upload day | Days gained |
|---|---|
| fewer than 180 days | 6 |
| 180 to 364 days | 3 |
| 365 days or more | 0 |

### Questions answered

**Which date is read?** The background check date on the agreement, the date of the latest clear background check.

**What if the check is exactly 180 days old?** It is no longer fewer than 180 days, so the permit gains 3 days.

**What if it is exactly 365 days old?** It gains none.

**Hypothetical example.** Upload day 2026-09-05, background check date 2026-03-10: 179 days before, so the permit gains 6 days. A check dated 2026-03-09 is 180 days before and gains 3.
